intent.raw_query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC

experiences.name: Sunset Sailing & Snorkeling Around Santorini Caldera
experiences.description: Join a small-group catamaran cruise departing in the late afternoon around the volcanic caldera of Santorini. Snorkel in crystal-clear Aegean waters, visit the Red and White beaches, and enjoy a traditional Greek mezze spread with local wine on board as you watch the legendary Oia sunset from the sea.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour (Varvakios Agora)
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local food guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and shop for local spices and ingredients. This indoor-friendly tour is perfect for avoiding midday heat.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Morning Visit
experiences.description: Arrive early at the stunning Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete to enjoy its famous pink-tinged sand and shallow turquoise lagoons before the midday crowds and heat arrive. Wade across the shallow sandbar to the small island, collect sea glass, and swim in calm, warm waters. Pack a local picnic from a nearby bakery for a perfect morning escape.

experiences.name: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in a Cretan Village
experiences.description: Spend a morning in a family-run kitchen in a traditional Cretan village learning to prepare authentic dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and galaktoboureko (custard pastry). The class takes place indoors making it an ideal midday heat or rain alternative. Enjoy the meal you prepare with local raki and wine.

experiences.name: Evening Taverna Crawl in Nafplio Old Town
experiences.description: As temperatures cool in the evening, stroll through the charming Venetian old town of Nafplio and hop between traditional tavernas sampling local Peloponnesian specialties: grilled octopus, tomatokeftedes, fresh grilled fish, and local Nemea red wine. The cobblestone streets and neoclassical architecture create a magical atmosphere perfect for a leisurely evening of authentic Greek dining and culture.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Greece
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50. Clear customs, collect luggage, and take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 into central Athens — both budget-friendly options under €10. Check into your budget hostel or guesthouse in the Monastiraki or Psiri neighborhood.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed evening stroll through Monastiraki Square and the Plaka neighborhood. Explore the atmospheric streets, browse souvenir stalls, and get oriented with the city. Watch the sunset over the Acropolis from Monastiraki Square for free.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a quick snack at the airport
meals.lunch: Grab a gyros wrap from a street kiosk near the airport or in Monastiraki for €2–3
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local taverna in Psiri neighborhood — try souvlaki plate or moussaka for €7–10. Look for places with handwritten menus and locals dining inside.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 14:50 arrival. Use the Metro Line 3 (€9) or X95 bus (€6) from the airport to Syntagma Square. Validate your ticket before boarding. Book budget accommodation in advance — Monastiraki and Psiri areas offer great value and central location.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Acropolis early (opens at 8:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Admission is €20 but includes entry to several other archaeological sites. Explore the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and enjoy panoramic views over Athens.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk down to the Ancient Agora of Athens (included in the Acropolis combo ticket). Explore the well-preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Afterward, wander through the Monastiraki flea market for free browsing.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Thissio neighborhood for an evening walk along the pedestrian promenade with Acropolis views. Enjoy the lively atmosphere and grab a coffee at a local café.

meals.breakfast: Tiropita (cheese pie) and coffee from a local bakery near your hostel — €2–3
meals.lunch: Souvlaki or gyros from a street stand in Monastiraki — €2–4
meals.dinner: Traditional taverna dinner in Thissio or Psiri — try grilled octopus, Greek salad, and house wine for €10–13 per person

day_by_day.notes: Buy the €30 combo ticket at the Acropolis which covers 7 archaeological sites valid for 5 days — great value. Wear comfortable shoes and bring water. The Acropolis can be very hot by midday in June.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Archaeological Museum (€12 admission) — one of the world's greatest collections of Greek antiquities. Spend 2–3 hours exploring artifacts from prehistoric to Roman times.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the colorful Exarchia neighborhood — a bohemian, artsy district with independent bookshops, street art, and cheap cafés. Visit the nearby Strefi Hill for free city views.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Central Market (Varvakios Agora) area for an authentic local evening experience. Browse the surrounding streets and grab dinner at one of the no-frills eateries popular with locals.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts from a local café — €3–4
meals.lunch: Spanakopita (spinach pie) and fresh juice from a bakery in Exarchia — €3–5
meals.dinner: Eat at a local eatery (estiatorio) near the Central Market — try the daily special (mageirefta) for €6–8, which includes a main dish, bread, and water

day_by_day.notes: The National Archaeological Museum is closed on Mondays — check the schedule. Exarchia is safe for tourists during the day and early evening. The Central Market area has some of Athens' most authentic and affordable dining.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning ferry from Piraeus port to the island of Aegina (about 1 hour, €8–10 each way). Explore the charming port town, visit the local market, and try fresh pistachios — Aegina is famous for them.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle (€5–8/day) or take a local bus to the Temple of Aphaia — a remarkably preserved ancient temple with sea views. Afterward, head to one of Aegina's quiet beaches like Agia Marina for a swim.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Piraeus in the late afternoon/early evening. Take the Metro back to central Athens and enjoy a quiet evening in the Plaka neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Grab a koulouri (sesame bread ring) and coffee at Piraeus port before boarding — €2
meals.lunch: Fresh grilled fish at a harbourside taverna in Aegina town — ask for the catch of the day, budget €10–14
meals.dinner: Simple dinner back in Athens — try a mezze spread (dips, olives, pita) at a local ouzeri for €8–10

day_by_day.notes: Ferries from Piraeus to Aegina run frequently. Take the Metro Line 1 (Green) from Monastiraki to Piraeus (€1.20). Bring sunscreen and a swimsuit. June weather is ideal for island day trips — expect around 23°C and mostly sunny skies.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take the KTEL bus from Athens to Nafplio (about 2.5 hours, €13–15). Nafplio is a stunning coastal town in the Peloponnese and a great budget base. Check into a budget guesthouse.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Nafplio's beautiful old town on foot — stroll along the waterfront promenade, visit Syntagma Square, and admire the Venetian architecture. Climb up to the Acronauplia fortress for free panoramic views.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the seaside and enjoy the sunset. Explore the narrow old town streets and browse local shops selling olive oil products and ceramics.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your Athens hostel or grab pastries at a bakery before the bus — €2–3
meals.lunch: Eat on the bus or grab a quick bite at the Nafplio bus station upon arrival — €3–5
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional taverna in Nafplio's old town — try fresh seafood pasta or grilled lamb chops for €9–12

day_by_day.notes: KTEL buses depart from Athens' Kifissos Bus Terminal (Terminal A). Take bus 051 from Omonia Square to reach the terminal. Book bus tickets in advance online or arrive early. Nafplio is one of Greece's most beautiful towns and very walkable.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the ancient theatre of Epidaurus (about 30 km from Nafplio, €12 admission). Take a local KTEL bus or join a budget group tour. The acoustics of this 4th-century BC theatre are legendary — test them yourself.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Nafplio and spend the afternoon at Arvanitia Beach — a small, rocky beach just a 10-minute walk from the old town, free to access. Swim in the crystal-clear Argolic Gulf waters.
day_by_day.evening: Climb the 999 steps up to the Palamidi Fortress (€8 admission, or go at sunset for dramatic lighting). Enjoy sweeping views over Nafplio and the bay.

meals.breakfast: Greek coffee and bougatsa (custard pastry) at a local café in Nafplio — €3–4
meals.lunch: Picnic lunch from the local market — olives, feta, bread, tomatoes, and fruit for €4–6
meals.dinner: Grilled octopus and Greek salad at a waterfront taverna in Nafplio — €10–13

day_by_day.notes: The Palamidi Fortress can also be reached by car or taxi if the steps are too strenuous. Arvanitia Beach has a small café. Epidaurus also hosts a famous summer festival — check if any performances coincide with your visit (tickets from €15).

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Nafplio to Thessaloniki by bus and train combination, or take a direct KTEL bus (approximately 5–6 hours, €25–35). Alternatively, travel back to Athens and take the train north. Check into a budget hostel in Thessaloniki's city center.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin exploring Thessaloniki on foot. Walk along the famous Thessaloniki waterfront (Nikis Avenue), visit the iconic White Tower (€4 admission), and explore the surrounding gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Ladadika district — a lively neighborhood of converted warehouses now filled with bars, restaurants, and cafés. Enjoy the vibrant evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your Nafplio guesthouse or grab food before departure — €2–4
meals.lunch: Eat on the road — pack snacks or stop at a roadside café — €4–6
meals.dinner: Dinner in Ladadika — try local Thessaloniki specialties like bougiourdi (baked feta with tomatoes) and grilled meats for €9–12

day_by_day.notes: Thessaloniki is Greece's second-largest city and has a distinct culture, cuisine, and vibe from Athens. The city is very walkable. Budget hostels in the city center are plentiful and affordable (€15–25/night for a dorm bed).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Archaeological Museum of Thessaloniki (€8 admission) — home to extraordinary finds from the royal tombs of Vergina, including gold artifacts from the Macedonian kingdom. Allow 2 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Upper Town (Ano Poli) — a beautifully preserved Ottoman-era neighborhood with Byzantine walls, old houses, and stunning views over the city and the Thermaic Gulf. Entry is free.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the bustling Modiano and Kapani covered markets for an authentic local experience. Browse fresh produce, spices, and local products. Have dinner in the market area.

meals.breakfast: Thessaloniki-style bougatsa (cream-filled pastry) at a traditional bougatsa shop — a must-try local specialty for €2–3
meals.lunch: Souvlaki or gyros from a local grill shop near the market — €2–4
meals.dinner: Dinner at a traditional ouzeri near Modiano Market — try a selection of mezedes (small dishes) with ouzo for €10–13

day_by_day.notes: Thessaloniki is considered the food capital of Greece — take every opportunity to try local specialties. The city's street food scene is excellent and very affordable. Ano Poli is best explored on foot but involves steep hills.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Halkidiki — the three-pronged peninsula southeast of Thessaloniki with some of Greece's most beautiful beaches. Take a KTEL Halkidikis bus (€5–8 each way) to Kassandra peninsula.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon at one of Kassandra's stunning beaches — Sani, Kallithea, or Possidi Beach. The water is clear and warm (around 22–23°C in June). Relax, swim, and enjoy the scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Thessaloniki by bus in the late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxed evening walk along the waterfront and watch the sunset over the Thermaic Gulf.

meals.breakfast: Grab pastries and coffee before catching the bus — €2–3
meals.lunch: Beach taverna lunch in Halkidiki — fresh grilled fish or seafood salad for €10–14
meals.dinner: Budget dinner back in Thessaloniki — try a local pita wrap shop or a cheap taverna for €6–9

day_by_day.notes: KTEL Halkidikis buses depart from a separate terminal in Thessaloniki (not the main KTEL terminal). Bring sunscreen, a towel, and water. June is an excellent time to visit Halkidiki before the peak July–August crowds arrive.

day_by_day.morning: Travel from Thessaloniki to Meteora by train or bus (approximately 3–4 hours, €10–20). Meteora is a UNESCO World Heritage Site featuring monasteries perched atop dramatic rock pillars. Check into a budget guesthouse in Kalambaka town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin exploring Meteora on foot or by renting a bicycle (€8–10/day). Visit the first set of monasteries — the Great Meteoron and Varlaam Monastery (€3 each). The views are absolutely breathtaking.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from one of the free viewpoints overlooking the rock formations — Psaropetra or the Doupiani Rock viewpoint are spectacular. Return to Kalambaka for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your Thessaloniki hostel or grab food at the station — €2–4
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic lunch from a local shop in Kalambaka — bread, cheese, olives, and fruit for €4–6
meals.dinner: Traditional Greek dinner in Kalambaka — try lamb kleftiko or stuffed peppers at a local taverna for €8–11

day_by_day.notes: Meteora monasteries have a dress code — shoulders and knees must be covered. Sarongs are sometimes available at the entrance. The rock formations are best photographed in the golden hour light. Kalambaka is a small, affordable town with good budget accommodation options.

day_by_day.morning: Continue exploring Meteora — visit the remaining monasteries including Roussanou, Agios Nikolaos Anapafsas, and Agios Stefanos (€3 each). Each offers unique architecture and different perspectives of the landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike one of the free walking trails through the Meteora rock formations. The trail from Kalambaka to the monasteries takes about 2–3 hours and offers incredible views. Alternatively, take a free viewpoint tour by local bus.
day_by_day.evening: Travel back toward Athens by train or bus (approximately 4–5 hours, €15–25). Arrive in Athens in the evening and check back into a budget hostel.

meals.breakfast: Greek yogurt, honey, and coffee at a café in Kalambaka — €3–4
meals.lunch: Grilled meat and salad at a simple taverna in Kalambaka before departure — €7–9
meals.dinner: Grab a gyros or souvlaki wrap upon arriving back in Athens — €2–4

day_by_day.notes: Check train and bus schedules in advance as connections from Meteora can be limited. The train journey through the Thessaly plain is scenic. If time allows, consider an afternoon departure to maximize time at Meteora.

day_by_day.morning: Take a ferry from Piraeus to the island of Hydra (approximately 1.5–2 hours, €15–20 each way by hydrofoil). Hydra is a car-free island with a stunning harbor, crystal-clear waters, and a relaxed atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Hydra town on foot — visit the harbor, the historic mansions, and the small Byzantine Museum (free). Hike or take a water taxi (€5–10) to one of the island's secluded swimming spots like Vlychos or Kamini beach.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the magical atmosphere of Hydra harbor at sunset — watch the donkeys (the island's only transport) and fishing boats. Take the late afternoon hydrofoil back to Piraeus.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and pastry near Piraeus port before boarding — €2–3
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch at a harbourside restaurant in Hydra — grilled fish or shrimp saganaki for €12–16
meals.dinner: Back in Athens — dinner at a budget taverna in Monastiraki or Psiri for €8–11

day_by_day.notes: Hydra is one of Greece's most beautiful and unique islands. No motorized vehicles are allowed — only donkeys, horses, and boats. It's slightly pricier than other islands but worth a day trip. Book hydrofoil tickets in advance in June.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — revisit your favorite spots or explore anything you missed. Visit the Benaki Museum (€9) for an overview of Greek culture from prehistory to modern times, or browse the Monastiraki flea market for last-minute souvenirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Last-minute souvenir shopping in Monastiraki — look for olive oil products, honey, herbs, and handmade ceramics as affordable and authentic gifts. Pack your bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Athens International Airport for your return flight. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure. Reflect on 13 incredible days exploring Greece's history, beaches, and food culture.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — tiropita, spanakopita, and Greek coffee at a local bakery — €3–5
meals.lunch: Last souvlaki or gyros in Monastiraki — a fitting farewell meal for €2–4
meals.dinner: Grab a meal at the airport or eat before heading to the airport — budget €8–12

day_by_day.notes: Take the Metro Line 3 from Monastiraki or Syntagma to the airport (€9, about 40 minutes). Keep some euros for airport snacks and any last transport costs. Check your airline's baggage policy if you've purchased souvenirs. Greece's 23°C June weather makes for a perfect final day.

trip_options.title: Classic Greece Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour (Varvakios Agora)
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local food guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and shop for local spices and ingredients. This indoor-friendly tour is perfect for avoiding midday heat.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival & transfer — Flight lands at 14:50, so morning is in transit. No morning activity scheduled.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) around 14:50, clear customs and collect luggage. Take the X95 express bus or Metro Line 3 to central Athens (~40 min, budget-friendly). Check into your mid-range hotel in the Monastiraki or Plaka neighborhood. Take a gentle orientation stroll through Monastiraki Square and the surrounding streets to get your bearings and shake off travel fatigue.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric Plaka district as the sun sets. Climb to a rooftop bar near Monastiraki for your first view of the illuminated Acropolis — a magical introduction to Athens. Keep the evening relaxed after a long travel day.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick gyros wrap (€3–4) from a street kiosk near Monastiraki Square shortly after check-in.
meals.dinner: Taverna Monastiri or a similar traditional taverna in Plaka — try Greek salad, tzatziki, grilled souvlaki, and a glass of local wine. Budget ~€18–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Prioritize hydration and a good night's sleep. Average high is 23°C, so evenings are pleasant for walking.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour (Varvakios Agora) — Join a guided food tour of the historic central market starting early (around 9:00 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Taste olives, cheeses, cured meats, fresh herbs, and local delicacies with a knowledgeable local guide. This is a highlight for food lovers and gives deep insight into Greek culinary culture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Acropolis and Acropolis Museum. Climb to see the Parthenon, Erechtheion, and sweeping city views (book tickets online in advance, ~€20). Afterward, spend an hour in the world-class Acropolis Museum (~€10) to see original friezes and artifacts in an air-conditioned setting.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the trendy Psyrri neighborhood adjacent to Monastiraki for dinner and a relaxed evening. Browse street art, small galleries, and lively squares.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at your hotel or a neighborhood café — Greek yogurt with honey and walnuts, freddo espresso. ~€5–8.
meals.lunch: Snacks and tastings are included during the Varvakios food tour. Supplement with a spanakopita (spinach pie) from a local bakery if still hungry. ~€2–3.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Psyrri — try Taverna tou Psyrri or similar. Order lamb chops (paidakia), horta (wild greens), and local Assyrtiko white wine. ~€20–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets online to skip the queue. Wear comfortable shoes — the Acropolis involves uneven marble surfaces. Bring sunscreen and a hat.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Ancient Agora of Athens (~€10), the heart of ancient Athenian civic life. Explore the remarkably preserved Temple of Hephaestus and the Stoa of Attalos museum. Arrive by 9:00 AM for cooler temperatures and fewer crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the tram or a short taxi to the Athens Riviera. Spend the afternoon at Vouliagmeni Lake or Asteras Beach — a beautiful, clean beach about 25 km from central Athens. Swim in the clear Aegean waters (average sea temp ~22°C in June). Sun lounger rental ~€8–12.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Athens. Explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood for an evening aperitif. Try a glass of ouzo or tsipouro with complimentary mezedes at a traditional ouzeri.

meals.breakfast: At your hotel or a neighborhood café — tiropita (cheese pie) and Greek coffee. ~€5–7.
meals.lunch: Beach taverna near Vouliagmeni — fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and cold beer. ~€18–22 per person.
meals.dinner: Light mezedes dinner in Kolonaki — order a spread of dips (taramosalata, melitzanosalata), grilled octopus, and fresh bread. ~€15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Athens Riviera is easily accessible by tram from Syntagma Square. June weather is ideal for beach days — warm but not yet peak summer heat.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Santorini — take an early morning high-speed ferry from Piraeus Port (book in advance, ~€45–60, ~5 hours) or a short domestic flight (~€60–90, 45 min). Enjoy the Aegean scenery en route. Arrive in Santorini (Thira) by early afternoon.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into your mid-range hotel in Fira or Imerovigli. After settling in, explore Fira town on foot — browse the clifftop walkway, visit the Museum of Prehistoric Thera (~€6), and soak in the iconic caldera views.
day_by_day.evening: Walk the famous caldera path from Fira toward Imerovigli (about 3 km, 1 hour) as the sun begins to lower. Find a clifftop spot to watch the legendary Santorini sunset. Return to Fira for dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — grab a bougatsa (custard pastry) and coffee from a Piraeus bakery. ~€4–6.
meals.lunch: Light snack on the ferry — bring your own or purchase from the ferry café. ~€8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Fira — try Mama's House or a similar mid-range taverna. Order fresh tomato fritters (tomatokeftedes), fava dip, and local Santorinian Assyrtiko wine. ~€22–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book ferry tickets well in advance for June travel. High-speed ferries (SeaJets, Hellenic Seaways) are faster but pricier. Santorini accommodation fills up fast — confirm your booking.

day_by_day.morning: Rent an ATV or scooter (~€20–30/day) and explore the island independently. Head to Oia village in the north — wander the iconic blue-domed churches, narrow whitewashed alleys, and art galleries. Arrive early (before 10 AM) to beat the tour groups.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive south to the Red Beach (Kokkini Paralia) near Akrotiri — one of Santorini's most dramatic beaches with striking red volcanic cliffs. Swim and relax (~€8 for a sun lounger). Afterward, visit the prehistoric ruins of Akrotiri (~€12), a remarkably preserved Bronze Age settlement buried by the volcanic eruption.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Oia for the world-famous sunset (arrive by 7:00 PM to secure a good spot — it gets very crowded). Afterward, have a romantic dinner in Oia.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café in Fira — Greek yogurt, honey, fresh fruit, and coffee. ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Beachside snack bar near Red Beach — grilled corn, fresh juice, or a simple sandwich. ~€8–10.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Oia — try Roka Restaurant or similar. Fresh seafood pasta, local wine, and caldera views. ~€28–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: ATV/scooter rental requires a valid license. Roads in Santorini are narrow and winding — drive carefully. Red Beach requires a short rocky walk from the parking area.

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning boat tour of the Santorini caldera (~€25–35). Visit the active volcanic island of Nea Kameni, hike to the crater, and swim in the therapeutic hot springs of Palea Kameni. Tours depart from Fira's old port (accessible by cable car or donkey path).
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at Perissa or Perivolos Beach on the island's southeast coast — long stretches of distinctive black volcanic sand with clear water and beach bars. Swim, sunbathe, and recharge.
day_by_day.evening: Back in Fira, explore the local shops and pick up Santorinian products — local wine, capers, and fava beans make great souvenirs. Enjoy a relaxed final evening on the island.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Fira before the boat tour — scrambled eggs, toast, and freddo cappuccino. ~€8–10.
meals.lunch: Beach taverna at Perivolos — grilled calamari, Greek salad, and cold Mythos beer. ~€16–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Fira — try Sphinx Restaurant or a similar mid-range spot. Order moussaka, stuffed peppers, and local wine. ~€20–26 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the caldera boat tour the day before or through your hotel. Morning departures are cooler and less crowded. Perissa beach has free public access alongside paid lounger areas.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Mykonos — take a high-speed ferry from Santorini to Mykonos (~2.5–3 hours, ~€40–55). Book in advance. Enjoy the Aegean crossing and arrive by midday.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into your mid-range hotel (Mykonos Town or nearby). Explore Mykonos Town (Chora) on foot — get delightfully lost in the labyrinthine whitewashed alleys designed to confuse pirates. Visit the iconic windmills at Kato Mili for panoramic views and photos.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Little Venice — the row of colorful houses built on the water's edge. Watch the sunset from here with a cocktail in hand. Explore the lively waterfront and Matogianni Street boutiques.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at your Santorini hotel before departure. ~€8–10.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch in Mykonos Town after arrival — try a local gyros or a souvlaki wrap from a street spot. ~€5–8.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Mykonos Town — try Nikos Taverna (a beloved local institution). Order fresh fish, dakos salad, and local wine. ~€25–32 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Mykonos is pricier than other Greek islands — budget slightly more for meals and activities here. Ferry schedules between Santorini and Mykonos vary; confirm times in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Take a short boat excursion to the sacred island of Delos (~€20 round trip + €12 entry). This UNESCO World Heritage Site is one of the most important archaeological sites in Greece — birthplace of Apollo and Artemis. Explore the ancient ruins, mosaics, and the famous Terrace of the Lions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Mykonos and head to Paradise Beach or Platis Gialos Beach for an afternoon of swimming and relaxation. Platis Gialos is more family-friendly and less party-oriented than Paradise Beach — great for a balanced beach afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mykonos Town for the evening. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere — Mykonos comes alive at night. Have dinner and then explore the nightlife scene at your own pace.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café in Mykonos Town — Greek yogurt with local thyme honey, fresh orange juice. ~€8–12.
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Platis Gialos — grilled octopus, tzatziki, and a cold drink. ~€18–22 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Mykonos Town — try M-eating or a similar quality mid-range restaurant. Fresh seafood, local cheeses, and Cycladic wine. ~€28–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Delos boats depart from the Old Port of Mykonos Town, typically at 9:00 AM and 10:00 AM. The site has no shade — bring a hat, sunscreen, and water. Last boat back is usually around 3:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or use the local bus (KTEL) to explore the quieter side of Mykonos. Visit Ano Mera village in the island's interior — a refreshingly authentic contrast to touristy Chora. See the 16th-century Panagia Tourliani Monastery and browse the small local market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Elia Beach — Mykonos's longest beach, with crystal-clear water and a more relaxed vibe. Swim, snorkel, and enjoy the afternoon sun. Sun loungers available for rent (~€10–15).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Mykonos — revisit Little Venice for sunset cocktails, then have a farewell dinner. Pack your bags for the next morning's departure.

meals.breakfast: Café breakfast in Mykonos Town — tiropita, coffee, and fresh juice. ~€7–10.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a taverna in Ano Mera village — very local, very affordable. Try the village salad and grilled lamb. ~€14–18 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner near Little Venice — fresh grilled fish of the day, capers salad, and local wine. ~€25–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ano Mera is about 8 km from Mykonos Town — easily reached by bus or scooter. The village offers a genuine slice of island life away from the tourist crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Crete — take a ferry or short flight from Mykonos to Heraklion, Crete (ferry ~7–8 hours overnight or daytime; flight ~45 min, ~€60–90). If taking a daytime ferry, enjoy the scenic Aegean crossing. Check into your mid-range hotel in Heraklion or the charming old town of Chania.
day_by_day.afternoon: If arriving in Heraklion, visit the Palace of Knossos (~€15) — the legendary Minoan palace complex, one of Europe's oldest cities. Explore the reconstructed frescoes and labyrinthine ruins with an audio guide.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Heraklion or transfer to Chania (2.5 hours by bus). Explore the Venetian harbor area of whichever city you're based in. Enjoy the warm evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — hotel or a quick café stop. ~€6–8.
meals.lunch: On the ferry or a quick bite after arrival. ~€10–14.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a harbourside taverna in Heraklion or Chania — try dakos (Cretan rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and local Cretan wine or raki. ~€20–26 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Crete is Greece's largest island with much more to explore. Consider basing yourself in Chania for its beautiful old town, or Heraklion for easier access to Knossos. Book accommodation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Chania Old Town (or Heraklion's old city if based there) — wander the Venetian harbor, the covered market (Agora), and the narrow streets of the old Jewish quarter. Visit the Archaeological Museum of Chania (~€4) for Minoan artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Elafonisi Beach (~1.5 hours from Chania by bus or rental car) — one of Greece's most stunning beaches, with pink-tinged sand and shallow turquoise lagoons. Swim and relax in this near-paradise setting. Alternatively, visit the closer Falasarna Beach (~1 hour) for equally beautiful clear water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Chania for the evening. Explore the atmospheric backstreets of the old town, browse local shops for Cretan olive oil, herbs, and honey.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Cretan breakfast at a café in Chania old town — barley rusks with tomato and cheese (dakos), local honey, and Cretan coffee. ~€7–10.
meals.lunch: Beachside snack at Elafonisi — bring a packed lunch or buy from the small beach kiosk. ~€8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Chania old town — try Tamam Restaurant (in a converted Turkish bath) or similar. Order lamb with artichokes, Cretan cheeses, and local wine. ~€22–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Elafonisi is a protected nature reserve — no water sports or loud music. The lagoon is very shallow (knee-deep in places), making it ideal for a relaxed swim. Arrive early to secure a good spot.

day_by_day.morning: Hike the famous Samaria Gorge (~€5 entry) — one of Europe's longest gorges at 16 km. The hike takes 4–6 hours and ends at the seaside village of Agia Roumeli. Buses depart from Chania early morning (~6:30–8:00 AM). The gorge is spectacular — towering cliffs, wild flowers, and mountain streams.
day_by_day.afternoon: Upon completing the gorge hike, arrive at Agia Roumeli beach — a well-earned swim in the Libyan Sea. Take the ferry from Agia Roumeli to Hora Sfakion (~€15, 1 hour), then a bus back to Chania.
day_by_day.evening: Rest and recover after the gorge hike — a well-deserved relaxed evening. Enjoy a quiet dinner and early night.

meals.breakfast: Very early breakfast before departure — energy-rich foods: eggs, bread, fruit. Pack snacks and plenty of water for the hike. ~€6–8.
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch for the gorge — sandwiches, nuts, fruit, and lots of water. There are no food stops inside the gorge.
meals.dinner: Celebratory dinner in Chania after the hike — treat yourself to a full Cretan feast: grilled lamb chops, horta, tzatziki, and a carafe of local wine. ~€22–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Samaria Gorge is strenuous — wear proper hiking shoes (not sandals), bring 2+ liters of water, sunscreen, and a light jacket for the cool gorge interior. The hike is one-way (downhill). Not suitable for those with knee problems.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Crete — visit the Venetian Lighthouse and walk the full length of Chania's beautiful harbor one last time. Browse the Chania covered market for last-minute food souvenirs: Cretan olive oil, thyme honey, dried herbs, and local cheeses (graviera, anthotyros).
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight, spend the afternoon at a nearby beach — Kalathas or Stavros Beach (where Zorba the Greek was filmed) are both within 15–20 minutes of Chania. Enjoy a final swim in the Aegean. Transfer to Chania Airport (CHQ) or Heraklion Airport (HER) for your return flight.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — fly home from Crete. Reflect on 13 incredible days of Greek beaches, ancient history, and unforgettable food.

meals.breakfast: Final Greek breakfast — yogurt with honey, fresh fruit, and a strong Greek coffee at a harbor café in Chania. ~€8–10.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a beachside taverna before heading to the airport — fresh fish, salad, and a cold drink. ~€16–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal, or an early dinner before departure if time allows.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before your flight for airport check-in and security. Chania Airport is small but can get busy in summer. Pack your olive oil and honey in checked luggage to avoid issues at security. Kalό taxίdi — safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Greece Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Sunset Sailing & Snorkeling Around Santorini Caldera
experiences.description: Join a small-group catamaran cruise departing in the late afternoon around the volcanic caldera of Santorini. Snorkel in crystal-clear Aegean waters, visit the Red and White beaches, and enjoy a traditional Greek mezze spread with local wine on board as you watch the legendary Oia sunset from the sea.

experiences.name: Athens Central Market Food Tour (Varvakios Agora)
experiences.description: Explore the historic Varvakios Agora (Athens Central Market) with a local food guide in the cool morning hours. Taste cured meats, fresh cheeses, olives, loukoumades (honey donuts), and spanakopita. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and shop for local spices and ingredients. This indoor-friendly tour is perfect for avoiding midday heat.

experiences.name: Elafonissi Beach Morning Visit
experiences.description: Arrive early at the stunning Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete to enjoy its famous pink-tinged sand and shallow turquoise lagoons before the midday crowds and heat arrive. Wade across the shallow sandbar to the small island, collect sea glass, and swim in calm, warm waters. Pack a local picnic from a nearby bakery for a perfect morning escape.

experiences.name: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in a Cretan Village
experiences.description: Spend a morning in a family-run kitchen in a traditional Cretan village learning to prepare authentic dishes such as dakos (barley rusk salad), lamb with stamnagathi greens, and galaktoboureko (custard pastry). The class takes place indoors making it an ideal midday heat or rain alternative. Enjoy the meal you prepare with local raki and wine.

experiences.name: Evening Taverna Crawl in Nafplio Old Town
experiences.description: As temperatures cool in the evening, stroll through the charming Venetian old town of Nafplio and hop between traditional tavernas sampling local Peloponnesian specialties: grilled octopus, tomatokeftedes, fresh grilled fish, and local Nemea red wine. The cobblestone streets and neoclassical architecture create a magical atmosphere perfect for a leisurely evening of authentic Greek dining and culture.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 14:50
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Athens International Airport (Eleftherios Venizelos) at 14:50 on Air Serbia. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange private luxury transfer to your Athens city-center hotel (e.g., Hotel Grande Bretagne or similar 5-star property on Syntagma Square). Check in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome drink at the rooftop bar overlooking the Acropolis.
day_by_day.evening: Take a leisurely evening stroll through the Plaka neighborhood — Athens' oldest district — winding through charming neoclassical streets and boutique shops. Enjoy a relaxed first dinner at a premium taverna.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or light snack at the airport
meals.dinner: Dinner at Strofi Restaurant near the Acropolis — a classic Athens institution with panoramic Acropolis views, serving refined Greek cuisine including lamb kleftiko, grilled octopus, and seasonal mezedes. Reserve a terrace table in advance.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance (Mercedes E-Class or similar). The Motel 6 listed in the booking details appears to be a placeholder — confirm your actual Athens luxury accommodation. Keep Day 1 light given travel fatigue.

day_by_day.morning: Athens Central Market Food Tour (Varvakios Agora): Join a small-group guided food tour of the historic Varvakios Agora starting at 9:00 AM before the heat builds. Explore stalls overflowing with fresh fish, cured meats, spices, olives, and local cheeses. Sample loukoumades (honey doughnuts), taramosalata, and aged graviera cheese with your expert local guide. Learn about Greek culinary traditions and the role of the agora in Athenian daily life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Acropolis and Parthenon (book skip-the-line tickets in advance). Explore the Acropolis Museum afterward — one of Europe's finest archaeological museums — with air-conditioned galleries housing original Parthenon friezes and Caryatid sculptures. Hire a private guide for a deeper experience.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at the rooftop bar of your hotel or at A for Athens rooftop bar in Monastiraki with sweeping Acropolis views. Then dinner in the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel's restaurant — Greek yogurt with Cretan thyme honey, fresh fruit, spanakopita, and cold-brew coffee
meals.lunch: Light mezedes lunch at a traditional ouzeri near the Central Market — try grilled sardines, tzatziki, and horiatiki salad with a glass of chilled Assyrtiko white wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Spondi (2 Michelin stars) in Pangrati — Athens' most celebrated fine-dining restaurant offering a creative Mediterranean tasting menu with impeccable wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Book Acropolis tickets and Spondi restaurant well in advance. Wear comfortable walking shoes and bring sun protection — June temperatures average 23°C but can feel warmer in direct sun.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Ancient Agora of Athens and the Temple of Hephaestus — one of the best-preserved ancient Greek temples. Explore the Stoa of Attalos museum. Afterward, wander through the Monastiraki flea market for artisan finds and vintage treasures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Athens by private transfer to Piraeus port (or domestic flight) and take a high-speed ferry to Nafplio in the Peloponnese — a 2.5-hour scenic journey. Alternatively, arrange a private car transfer (approximately 2 hours via the scenic coastal highway). Check into a luxury boutique hotel such as Nafplia Palace or 3sixty Hotel with panoramic views over the Argolic Gulf.
day_by_day.evening: Evening Taverna Crawl in Nafplio Old Town: As temperatures cool, stroll through the enchanting Venetian old town with its neoclassical mansions, bougainvillea-draped alleyways, and waterfront promenade. Hop between traditional tavernas sampling local Peloponnesian specialties — try grilled lamb chops, local feta, and Nemea red wine from the nearby wine region.

meals.breakfast: Lavish hotel breakfast buffet featuring local honey, fresh pastries, Greek cheeses, and seasonal fruit
meals.lunch: Lunch aboard the ferry or a quick stop at a seaside café in Piraeus — fresh grilled fish and a Greek salad
meals.dinner: Taverna crawl dinner across 2–3 stops in Nafplio Old Town — begin with mezedes at Aiolos, continue with grilled seafood at Savouras, and finish with dessert (galaktoboureko) and local tsipouro at a traditional kafeneion on Syntagma Square, Nafplio

day_by_day.notes: Nafplio is considered one of Greece's most romantic and beautiful towns. Book your boutique hotel well in advance for June. The evening taverna crawl works best starting around 8:00 PM when the old town comes alive.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning hike up to the Palamidi Fortress (999 steps or take a taxi to the top) for breathtaking panoramic views over Nafplio, the Argolic Gulf, and the surrounding mountains. Explore the seven bastions of this magnificent 18th-century Venetian fortification. Return to town and visit the small but excellent Bourtzi Castle on the islet in the harbor (short boat ride).
day_by_day.afternoon: Day trip by private car to the ancient site of Mycenae (45 minutes from Nafplio) — the legendary Bronze Age citadel of Agamemnon. Walk through the iconic Lion Gate, explore the Treasury of Atreus (beehive tomb), and visit the on-site museum. Return to Nafplio for a relaxing afternoon swim at Arvanitia Beach, a small rocky cove just below the old town walls.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on the waterfront promenade of Nafplio with a glass of chilled Moschofilero wine. Elegant dinner at a top restaurant in the old town.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at a traditional kafeneion on Nafplio's Syntagma Square — Greek coffee, koulouri (sesame bread ring), and tiropita (cheese pie)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a family taverna near Mycenae — slow-roasted lamb, village salad, and local bread baked in a wood-fired oven
meals.dinner: Dinner at Omorfo Tavernaki in Nafplio — a beloved upscale taverna known for its creative takes on Peloponnesian classics, including slow-cooked goat with orzo and fresh seafood from the Argolic Gulf

day_by_day.notes: Start the Palamidi hike early (before 9:00 AM) to avoid midday heat. Wear sturdy shoes. Mycenae is a UNESCO World Heritage Site — a private guide enhances the experience significantly.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Nafplio by private transfer to Kalamata Airport or Patras port for onward travel to Crete. Alternatively, take a scenic private car journey south through the Mani Peninsula — one of Greece's most dramatic and unspoiled landscapes — stopping at the medieval tower houses of Areopoli and the stunning Diros Caves (guided boat tour through illuminated stalactite caverns).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Crete (Chania or Heraklion) by afternoon ferry or short domestic flight. Private transfer to your luxury accommodation in the Chania region — consider Domes of Elounda, Amirandes Grecotel, or a private villa near Chania Old Town. Settle in and enjoy the pool or beach at your resort.
day_by_day.evening: First evening in Crete — explore the magical Venetian harbor of Chania Old Town at sunset. Walk along the lighthouse promenade, browse artisan shops selling Cretan olive oil, herbs, and leather goods, and soak in the atmosphere of one of Greece's most beautiful harbor towns.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Nafplio before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch en route — if passing through Mani, stop at a traditional kafeneion in Areopoli for Mani specialties: local sausages (loukaniko), sun-dried figs, and Mani olive oil drizzled on crusty bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tamam Restaurant in Chania Old Town — set inside a converted Ottoman bathhouse, serving creative Cretan-Mediterranean cuisine with exceptional local wine selection

day_by_day.notes: The Mani Peninsula detour adds approximately 3–4 hours but is highly recommended for its extraordinary scenery and cultural uniqueness. Book Diros Caves tickets in advance for June. Confirm your Crete accommodation well ahead of the peak season.

day_by_day.morning: Elafonissi Beach Morning Visit: Depart early (7:30 AM) by private car for the 1.5-hour drive to Elafonissi Beach in southwestern Crete. Arrive before the crowds to enjoy the famous pink-tinged sand (colored by crushed coral and shells), crystal-clear turquoise lagoons, and the shallow sandbar walk to the small islet. Swim, snorkel, and relax in one of the Mediterranean's most spectacular natural settings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return journey via the scenic Topolia Gorge and the charming village of Elos, known for its ancient chestnut trees. Stop at a local apiary to taste Cretan thyme honey — considered among the world's finest. Visit the Monastery of Chrysoskalitissa perched dramatically on a clifftop above the sea before heading back to Chania.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing evening at your Chania resort or hotel. Enjoy a private sunset cocktail on your terrace or at the hotel's infinity pool bar. Optional: book a traditional Cretan lyre music performance at a local cultural venue.

meals.breakfast: Early light breakfast at your hotel before departure — yogurt, honey, and fresh fruit to go
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch on the beach at Elafonissi — arrange a premium picnic basket through your hotel with local cheeses, Cretan dakos (rusk with tomato and feta), olives, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Thalassino Ageri in Chania — a romantic seafood restaurant perched on the rocks above the sea, serving the freshest catch of the day with exceptional Cretan white wines

day_by_day.notes: Elafonissi is a protected nature reserve — no umbrellas or sunbeds are available, so bring your own shade. Arrive before 9:00 AM to secure the best spots. The beach can get very crowded by midday in June. Bring reef-safe sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Traditional Greek Cooking Class in a Cretan Village: Join a family-run cooking class in a traditional village outside Chania (e.g., Vamos or Gavalochori). Spend the morning learning to prepare authentic Cretan dishes from scratch — make dakos, stuffed zucchini flowers, lamb with stamnagathi (wild greens), and loukoumades. Visit the family's garden and olive grove, and learn about the Cretan diet's role in longevity and health.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Venetian Old Town of Chania — explore the covered market (Agora), the Archaeological Museum housed in a former Venetian church, and the Maritime Museum of Crete. Browse the leather workshops on Skridlof Street for handmade sandals. Enjoy a leisurely afternoon coffee at a café overlooking the Venetian lighthouse.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar in Chania Old Town with views over the harbor and the White Mountains. Elegant dinner at one of Chania's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Enjoy the fruits of your cooking class — sit down with the host family to share the meal you prepared, accompanied by local Cretan wine and raki
meals.dinner: Dinner at Portes Restaurant in Chania Old Town — a sophisticated restaurant in a beautifully restored Venetian building, offering creative Cretan cuisine with an outstanding wine list featuring rare Cretan varietals

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class typically runs 9:00 AM–1:00 PM including the shared meal. Book in advance as classes fill quickly in June. This is one of the most memorable and immersive experiences of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Samaria Gorge — one of Europe's longest and most spectacular gorges (16 km). Begin the hike from the Omalos Plateau (private transfer arranged) and descend through towering rock walls, ancient pine forests, and past the abandoned village of Samaria. The hike takes 4–6 hours depending on pace. This is a moderately strenuous activity — wear proper hiking shoes and carry water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Emerge at the seaside village of Agia Roumeli at the bottom of the gorge. Cool off with a swim in the crystal-clear Libyan Sea. Take the ferry along the dramatic southern Cretan coastline to Sfakia, then private transfer back to Chania (approximately 1.5 hours). Return to your hotel for a well-deserved rest and spa treatment.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet, relaxing evening at your hotel. Optional in-room dining or a light dinner at the hotel restaurant. Book a 90-minute massage or couples' spa treatment to recover from the day's hike.

meals.breakfast: Early hearty hotel breakfast before the hike — eggs, protein, and carbohydrates for energy
meals.lunch: Lunch at a taverna in Agia Roumeli after completing the gorge — fresh grilled fish, Greek salad, and cold Mythos beer (well deserved!)
meals.dinner: Light in-room dining or hotel restaurant — a mezedes platter, fresh bread, and a glass of Cretan red wine

day_by_day.notes: The Samaria Gorge is open from May 1 to October 31. Entrance fee applies. The gorge closes if there is heavy rain — check conditions the day before. This is a full-day commitment. Alternatively, if hiking is not preferred, substitute with a private boat charter along the Chania coastline visiting sea caves and secluded beaches.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Crete by domestic flight (Chania to Santorini, approximately 45 minutes) or high-speed ferry. Private transfer to your luxury accommodation in Oia or Imerovigli — consider Canaves Oia Epitome, Grace Hotel Santorini, or Mystique — all offering iconic caldera views and infinity pools. Check in and spend the morning exploring the iconic blue-domed churches and whitewashed alleys of Oia village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the volcanic island at your own pace — visit the village of Pyrgos (Santorini's highest point) for panoramic island views, or take a private wine tour of Santorini's unique volcanic vineyards. Visit Santo Wines or Domaine Sigalas for a premium tasting of Assyrtiko, Nykteri, and Vinsanto wines paired with local cheeses and cherry tomatoes.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset Sailing & Snorkeling Around Santorini Caldera: Board a luxury small-group catamaran in the late afternoon for a sunset cruise around the volcanic caldera. Snorkel at the hot springs near Nea Kameni volcanic island, swim in the caldera's warm waters, and watch the legendary Santorini sunset from the water with a glass of chilled Assyrtiko in hand. Light snacks and drinks included on board.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Chania before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a cliffside restaurant in Oia — try fresh tuna carpaccio, grilled calamari, and fava (yellow split pea purée) with capers — a Santorini specialty
meals.dinner: Dinner at Lauda Restaurant at Andronis Luxury Suites in Oia — one of Santorini's most celebrated fine-dining experiences, offering a creative Mediterranean tasting menu with caldera views and an exceptional Greek wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book the catamaran sunset cruise well in advance — June is peak season and spots fill up fast. The Santorini sunset from the water is arguably more spectacular than from the crowded Oia castle viewpoint. Confirm your luxury hotel booking months ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of ancient Akrotiri — the remarkably preserved Minoan Bronze Age city buried by the Santorini volcanic eruption around 1600 BC. Often called the 'Pompeii of the Aegean,' the site features multi-story buildings, sophisticated drainage systems, and stunning frescoes. Afterward, visit the Red Beach (Kokkini Paralia) nearby — a dramatic beach of deep red volcanic cliffs and dark sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to your hotel for a luxurious afternoon at the infinity pool overlooking the caldera. Alternatively, arrange a private helicopter tour of the Santorini caldera and surrounding Cycladic islands (30–45 minutes) for a truly unforgettable aerial perspective. Enjoy a spa treatment at your hotel's wellness center.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the romantic alleys of Oia village as the golden hour light transforms the whitewashed buildings. Browse high-end art galleries and jewelry boutiques. Watch the sunset from the Byzantine Castle ruins in Oia (arrive 30 minutes early to secure a good spot).

meals.breakfast: Breakfast on your private terrace or balcony — fresh fruit, Greek yogurt with Santorini cherry tomato jam, eggs, and freshly squeezed orange juice with caldera views
meals.lunch: Lunch at Metaxy Mas in Exo Gonia — a beloved local taverna away from the tourist crowds, serving exceptional traditional Santorinian cuisine including fava, white eggplant salad, and slow-cooked lamb
meals.dinner: Dinner at Selene Restaurant in Pyrgos — Santorini's most iconic fine-dining institution, celebrating Cycladic gastronomy with a seasonal tasting menu featuring local ingredients: Santorini fava, cherry tomatoes, capers, and fresh seafood

day_by_day.notes: Akrotiri requires advance ticket booking. The Red Beach involves a short rocky walk — wear appropriate footwear. Oia gets extremely crowded at sunset — consider watching from Imerovigli or Skaros Rock for a more peaceful experience.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure — enjoy a long, indulgent breakfast on your terrace. Take a private boat charter to the uninhabited island of Thirassia (Santorini's quieter sister island) for a peaceful morning swim in secluded coves and a walk up to the traditional village of Manolas. Alternatively, visit the black sand beach of Perissa or Perivolos for a more relaxed beach day.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Santorini and visit Fira (the island's capital) — explore the Museum of Prehistoric Thera (housing original Akrotiri frescoes), browse the upscale boutiques along the caldera rim, and enjoy a coffee at a cliffside café. Take the traditional donkey path or cable car down to the old port of Fira Skala.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner on Santorini — choose one of the island's most spectacular dining settings for a memorable final evening on the island.

meals.breakfast: Luxurious hotel breakfast — smoked salmon, avocado, poached eggs, fresh pastries, and a Bloody Mary or fresh juice
meals.lunch: Seafood lunch at a taverna on Thirassia island or at a beachfront restaurant at Perivolos Beach — grilled whole sea bream, octopus salad, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Dinner at Argo Restaurant in Fira — a romantic cliffside restaurant with dramatic caldera views, serving refined Greek seafood and meat dishes with an extensive Santorinian wine list

day_by_day.notes: Private boat charters to Thirassia can be arranged through your hotel concierge. June weather is ideal for island hopping. This is a good day to purchase high-quality local products to bring home: Vinsanto wine, Santorini capers, and local saffron.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Santorini by high-speed ferry or domestic flight back to Athens. Private luxury transfer from the port or airport to your Athens hotel. Check in and freshen up. Visit the National Archaeological Museum — the world's finest collection of ancient Greek art, including the Antikythera Mechanism, the Mask of Agamemnon, and stunning bronze sculptures.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Kolonaki neighborhood — Athens' most fashionable district. Browse designer boutiques, visit the Benaki Museum (Greek cultural history from prehistoric times to the 20th century), and enjoy a coffee at a chic café on Kolonaki Square. Take the funicular up Lycabettus Hill for the best panoramic view of Athens, the Acropolis, and the Saronic Gulf.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Athens — a celebratory farewell dinner at one of the city's finest restaurants, followed by cocktails at a rooftop bar with Acropolis views.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Santorini hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at a stylish restaurant in Kolonaki — try Vezene or Aleria for creative modern Greek cuisine in an elegant setting
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Varoulko Seaside in Mikrolimano (Piraeus) — Chef Lefteris Lazarou's Michelin-starred seafood restaurant, widely regarded as one of Greece's greatest dining experiences. Tasting menu featuring the finest Aegean seafood with exceptional wine pairings.

day_by_day.notes: Book Varoulko Seaside well in advance — it is one of Greece's most sought-after reservations. The restaurant is located in Piraeus (30 minutes from central Athens by taxi) — arrange private transfer. The Lycabettus Hill funicular runs until late evening.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Athens — enjoy a leisurely breakfast at your hotel. Last-minute shopping for premium Greek products: extra virgin olive oil from Kalamata, aged Graviera cheese, Mastiha liqueur from Chios, handmade jewelry from Monastiraki, or a piece from a Kolonaki art gallery. Visit the Acropolis one final time at opening (8:00 AM) for a quieter, more contemplative experience if not visited earlier.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, enjoy a final Greek lunch in Athens. Private luxury transfer to Athens International Airport for your return flight on Air Serbia. Allow at least 3 hours before departure for international check-in.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Athens International Airport. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days of Greek beaches, world-class food, ancient history, and island magic.

meals.breakfast: Final indulgent hotel breakfast — Greek yogurt with Hymettus honey, fresh pastries, eggs any style, and strong Greek coffee
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at Diporto Agoras — a legendary, no-menu Athens institution hidden in the Central Market basement, serving whatever is fresh that day: chickpea soup, grilled fish, and house wine from the barrel. A perfect, authentic final meal.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Athens Airport has excellent duty-free shopping for last-minute Greek products. Confirm your Air Serbia flight details and check-in requirements. Keep all receipts for VAT refund claims on purchases over €50 (available at the airport). This concludes your 13-day premium Greece itinerary.

query: Greece under $2000, beaches and local food, summer, flying from NYC
